title: Record that the caller outside the selected pricing has no bit_saving input
body: ## Change and mathematical scope Negative result for one named caller. No new κ. The selected conditional exponent stays **781451/250000000**. The five framework assumptions remain. The recorded PR5679 component is ```text C = 3507410738409/1000000000000000 ``` from `research/g20-helper-split/ORDINARY-RESULT.json`, with `whole_kappa` null. This package does not reopen the selected pricing assembly's stock gate and does not change the cover inside that assembly. The caller outside that assembly is `physical` in `research/p104-productive-controller/caller.py`. The selected verifier loads that module and calls `C.physical(caller, word)` before `pricing.run`. The function's parameters are `word` and `local`, with no defaults and no parameter named `bit_saving`. At that call, the first argument is the controller returned by `construct()`, which the verifier requires to equal `CONTROLLER.json`. That object has no `bit_saving` field and does not contain the numerator of C. The second argument is the regenerated edited word held in the verifier's variable `word`. It is not the replay dictionary the verifier names `local`, and it is not C. `physical` contains one copy of each Gaussian check: "Multiply the Gaussian pair twice with exact real and imaginary parts." and "All idle Gaussian axes". Its only direct return statement builds a dictionary whose keys include `whole_idle_jobs` and do not include `bit_saving`. There is no `bit_saving` input that can be set to C, so this caller does not consume C. `physical` was not executed. No execution receipt is claimed. `pricing.run` is a different function. Its parameters are `local, native, word, physical`. Inside the body, after `atom > ordinary > admitted > TESTED`, it assigns `'bit_saving': admitted` and passes that dictionary to the PR4359 ledger. That assignment is the assembly already rejected for C. It is not this caller. At base commit `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, `git ls-tree -r --name-only` lists exactly 15 paths whose final component is `caller.py`. None of those blobs contains `bit_saving`. Exactly seven contain `Gaussian` or `gaussian`. Five of those seven are blob `6ac5e735691555ecafe2afbcff71edd923178113`, the named file and four retained copies. The other two, `research/native-involutive-dual/caller.py` and `research/physical-boundary-rhs-caller/caller.py`, do not define `physical`. This is an exhaustive finite census of that filename at that commit. It is not a proof that no function outside those files can accept C. ## Task and overlap Base commit `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` on canonical `CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds` main. This fork draft is based on `cursor/upstream-7c49fe32-pin-cc03`, which is that commit, so the diff is this package. It is not an upstream pull request and it does not change the selected frontier. Priority revision 8. Catalogue card `supplier-boundary-audit`. Scope status: **refined**. The card asks whether one changed supplier has complete native, caller, ordinary and outer admission coverage, and says to stop at one resolved gap. The gap taken here is the caller the selected verifier loads before `pricing.run`. The question is open question 2 of the note on discussion #1166, comment 19492491, recorded in fork PR 149. A neighbouring task owns a different cover inside the same ordinary formula. This package does not take that cover. Overlap at `2026-11-10T02:08:04Z` searched 885 open PR bodies and 6,934 discussion records, plus the local notes at `7c49fe32`. Status `POSSIBLE_OVERLAP_NOT_A_NOVELTY_CERTIFICATE`. The search hits the source comment, the PR5679 ordinary notes, and the income audit that uses this same `caller.py` for a different theorem. No open PR states this caller's parameter list. No matches is not proof that a hidden diff is absent. The family-status expansion gate was not opened. This package does not extend a construction. ## Validation Environment: Python 3.12, standard library, and local Git. Head `95659908a8cd692f54026cd69795a86d6b0067aa`. From the repository root: ```sh python3 -I -W error -B research/gaussian-caller-outside-pricing/verify.py python3 -I -O -W error -B research/gaussian-caller-outside-pricing/verify.py python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-caller-outside-pricing python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-caller-outside-pricing --check-source-history python3 -B scripts/research_selected_baseline.py ``` Observed: - both verifier modes print `PASS_GAUSSIAN_CALLER_OUTSIDE_PRICING`, with `bit_saving_input` null, `named_caller_consumes_C` false, and `physical_executed` false - the launcher prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` with outcome `negative-result` - the commit check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` for this head, with source history `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a` - the baseline check prints `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY` and still reports selected κ `781451/250000000` and admitted BIT `17/5000` Checks raise `SystemExit`, so `-O` does not disable them. Controls: an in-memory signature `physical(word, local, bit_saving)` is detected, and a snippet that calls `pricing.run` before `physical` is rejected. Not run: `physical`, the PR5679 caller replay, the pricing assembly, the outer ledger, native maps, compiler, tape, analytic recovery, `make frontier6030-verify`, Lean, and Docker. Unknown costs are not treated as zero. The baseline command is a source-binding orientation, not a scientific replay of this obstruction. ## Credit The caller and the selected verifier are DreamingOfClouds' PR #6030 chain, with the productive controller caller from the retained P104 lineage. The component C is Ali Romman's PR #5679, recorded in `research/g20-helper-split`. The assembly rejection of C inside the selected pricing is the earlier note on discussion #1166, not a result of this package. Dugongue, ai-nanachi, and the notices retained in those packages keep their credit. Prepared by unpaidmoon with substantial Cursor Grok assistance. Apache-2.0. ## Open next questions 1. Can a function that is not one of these 15 `caller.py` files, and is not `pricing.run`, accept C as a parameter named `bit_saving` while checking a Gaussian pair or idle Gaussian axis? First step: name that function from a file whose final component is not `caller.py` and whose path is not `research/p104-helper470-twin-rung-removal/pricing.py`, then execute it at C. Blocked by the absence of such a checked function. This census does not search other filenames, and it does not execute the ledger. ## Workflow feedback (optional) The selected verifier's variable `word` is the second argument of `physical(word, local)`, so the call `physical(caller, word)` has to be read against the signature before naming the inputs. A parameter named `word` is not, by itself, the edited word.
